title: Cloud Native Architecture: Containers, Kubernetes & 12-Factor App
source: IBM Cloud Architecture Center & Red Hat OpenShift Docs
content: Cloud-native architectures leverage containerization (Docker/OCI) and orchestration (Kubernetes, IBM Code Engine) for resilience and autoscaling. The Twelve-Factor App methodology mandates: declarative configuration stored in environment variables, stateless disposable processes, backing services treated as attached resources, and parity between development and production. Kubernetes concepts: Pods (smallest deployable units), Deployments (declarative replica management), and Services (stable network endpoints with built-in load balancing).
key_takeaways: Stateless microservices allow seamless horizontal scaling
Kubernetes controllers reconcile desired state with current state
Twelve-Factor principles minimize divergence across deployment targets

title: IBM Granite Foundation Models, RAG Architecture & watsonx
source: IBM watsonx.ai Technical Whitepaper & Granite Model Documentation
content: IBM Granite is a flagship family of open enterprise foundation models designed for enterprise language and code tasks, trained on rigorously curated business, academic, and code datasets. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) grounds Granite foundation models in external knowledge documents: 1. Ingestion & layout parsing using IBM Docling, 2. Dense semantic vector embedding generation using IBM Slate (ibm/slate-30m-english-rtr), 3. Vector similarity retrieval via cosine distance, 4. Prompt synthesis with context grounding to prevent hallucinations and provide verifiable source citations.
key_takeaways: IBM Granite provides transparent, enterprise-grade generative intelligence
Docling handles multiformat document layout and structured extraction
IBM Slate dense embeddings power high-precision semantic retrieval in RAG
